paper_metadata.title: Noise-Robust Quantum Generative Models for Distribution Learning and Efficient Data Loading

summary: The paper proposes noise-resilient gate-based qGANs for distribution learning on 6 qubits, reporting best noiseless Wasserstein distance 0.00271±0.00041 for EﬀSU2–WGAN-GP versus 0.0234±0.0048 for the RY–CZ baseline, and noisy p=0.02 performance of 0.0046±0.0004. It also validates a downstream 10-qubit QAE European call pricing workflow, obtaining 5.44±0.03 on simulator and 5.47±0.07 on IBM Boeblingen versus classical Monte Carlo 5.43±0.02.

experiments.description: Hybrid qGAN distribution-learning experiments on 2D Gaussian and log-normal targets using QCNN or EfficientSU2 generators with WGAN-GP or MMD losses, evaluated on noiseless simulation and noisy depolarizing simulation, with IBM Boeblingen hardware verification for the financial-loading/QAE workflow.

algorithm.variant: hybrid qGAN with WGAN-GP and MMD losses; QCNN and EfficientSU2 ansätze
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 500 epochs; plateau criterion used for convergence speed (generator loss and Wasserstein distance stable within ±0.002 for 20 consecutive epochs)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random seeds fixed; initial parameters not otherwise specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: target PDFs discretized on an 8x8 grid (64 bins) and loaded into a 6-qubit state; generator outputs measurement probabilities over the grid
problem_formulation.objective_function: WGAN-GP objective for distribution matching; MMD objective using FidelityQuantumKernel for kernel-based matching
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: gradient penalty for WGAN-GP; kernel MMD loss for multimodal matching; depolarizing noise injected on CX gates during noisy runs

problem_instance.description: Learning and loading 2D continuous probability distributions for synthetic data and financial log-normal returns; downstream European call pricing via QAE
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Gaussian generated with SciPy multivariate normal and normalized over 64 bins; log-normal asset returns discretized via affine mapping for efficient data loading; target PDFs flattened for metrics
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: mean ± std over 20 independent runs for noiseless results; 5 runs for noisy results; noise sweeps over p in [0, 0.05]; convergence speed measured by plateau criterion; statistical tests include Wilcoxon, KL, KS, and Wasserstein

implementation_details.transpilation_target: Qiskit circuit.library; SamplerQNN; TorchConnector; ParamShiftSamplerGradient; AerSampler
implementation_details.classical_solver: SciPy for Wasserstein and KS; PyTorch MLP discriminator
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: SciPy generation of target distributions; affine normalization; softmax normalization for discriminator inputs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Wasserstein, KL, KS, fidelity, t-SNE visualizations; statistical testing

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: MMD stable; WGAN-GP more volatile but decreasing

speedup_claims.baseline_method: exact quantum state preparation / classical loading
speedup_claims.conditions: qGAN distribution loading into n-qubit states
speedup_claims.caveats: Claimed for approximate loading; exact state preparation is stated to require O(2^n) gates.
This is a general QAE complexity claim referenced in the paper, not a direct complexity proof from the experiments.
Based on WS 0.00271 vs 0.0234; improvement is distribution-learning specific, not pricing-specific.
Reported for financial risk modeling (VaR), not directly for European call price.

speedup_claims.conditions: simulation for same precision in QAE pricing
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported in text/figure description; exact shot counts are not provided.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(poly(n)) for qGAN loading; O(sqrt(N)) for QAE downstream pricing
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(2^n) for exact state preparation; O(N) for classical Monte Carlo pricing

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 6 qubits for distribution learning; 1024 shots; noisy simulation plus limited IBM Boeblingen verification
limiting_factors: No clear end-to-end quantum advantage over classical baselines; classical MMD-GAN matches or beats some quantum variants on noiseless WS distance
Quadratic-style downstream speedup claims are not enough to establish practical advantage under Hoefler constant-factor analysis
Small problem size (6 qubits, 64 bins) and synthetic toy distributions
Noise sensitivity and hardware overhead on NISQ devices
Data loading remains the central bottleneck

notes: Hardware is mixed: noisy simulation via Qiskit/AerSampler and verification on IBM Boeblingen; no single QPU device name beyond IBM Boeblingen is given.

The paper reports 6 qubits for the distribution-learning qGAN and 10 qubits for the downstream QAE pricing circuit; the experiment entry focuses on the qGAN experiments, with QAE treated as a downstream application within the same study.
Circuit depth for QCNN is described structurally (2 convolution-pooling blocks) rather than as a numeric depth; EfficientSU2 depth is given by reps=4,6,8 with final reps=8.

The paper reports improved robustness and lower Wasserstein distance for EﬀSU2–WGAN-GP (0.00271±0.00041 noiseless), but classical MMD-GAN is comparable (0.0029±0.0006) and classical WGAN-GP is not uniformly dominated across all noisy settings.
This is a noisy-simulation plus limited hardware-validation study, not a demonstrated practical advantage.

experiments.description: European call option pricing using quantum amplitude estimation with qGAN-loaded log-normal distributions, evaluated on simulator and IBM Boeblingen hardware.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with qGAN-loaded log-normal distribution
algorithm.convergence_criteria: pricing accuracy evaluated at epsilon=0.01; no iterative convergence criterion reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: qGAN-loaded distribution from the trained generator; QAE initialization not otherwise specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: log-normal asset-return distribution loaded into a quantum state for amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: estimate European call option price via QAE from the loaded distribution

problem_instance.description: European call option pricing under Black-Scholes-style log-normal asset dynamics
problem_instance.dataset_name: European call option / log-normal asset return model
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: log-normal distribution generated from simulated asset returns and discretized for qGAN loading
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: comparison against classical Monte Carlo price; simulator and IBM Boeblingen hardware results reported; pricing error and shot-scaling compared

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on IBM superconducting device

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Q Boeblingen via Qiskit Runtime
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: qGAN-loaded log-normal distribution used as input to QAE
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: pricing error comparison; shot-scaling log-log analysis

speedup_claims.conditions: QAE pricing with qGAN-loaded log-normal distribution
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic quadratic speedup claim; the experiment reports empirical pricing values but not a formal complexity proof.
Reported in the text/figure caption; exact shot counts are not provided.
The paper states 25% error reduction on hardware, but the exact baseline used for this percentage is not fully specified.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 10 qubits for QAE pricing; IBM Boeblingen hardware and simulator results; 1024-shot qGAN loading context
limiting_factors: The pricing result is benchmarked against classical Monte Carlo, but the reported improvement is modest and tied to a small, problem-specific setup
The qGAN loader is itself a prerequisite and remains a bottleneck
No crossover analysis or scaling evidence is provided
Hardware results are on a small 20-qubit IBM device

notes: The paper explicitly states QAE on 10 qubits and IBM Boeblingen hardware.
No detailed QAE circuit depth, gate counts, or shot count for the pricing run are reported beyond the general 1024-shot SamplerQNN setting used in the qGAN training section.
The paper reports 5.44±0.03 on simulator and 5.47±0.07 on IBM Boeblingen versus classical Monte Carlo 5.43±0.02, i.e., close agreement rather than a clear advantage.
The result is best interpreted as a small-scale validation of QAE workflow, not demonstrated quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Baseline classical WGAN-GP and classical MMD-GAN comparisons reported in Tables 1 and 2 for distribution learning.
key_results: Table 1 (noiseless 2D Gaussian): Classical WGAN-GP WS=0.0079±0.0007, Rel. Entropy=0.440±0.051, KS p-value < 10^-6; Classical MMD-GAN WS=0.0029±0.0006, Rel. Entropy=0.108±0.021, KS p-value=0.146±0.093.

Table 2 (p=0.02 noise): Classical WGAN-GP WS=0.0038±0.0003, Rel. Entropy=0.6887±0.0365, KS p-value=0.0113±0.0206; Classical MMD-GAN WS=0.0046±0.0004, Rel. Entropy=0.3069±0.0232, KS p-value=0.2707±0.1261.
